source: reconstruction of the cache-mode bypass GitHub documents for low-trust triggers (issue #533)
note: The shape GitHub warns about when it documents cache-mode: an issue_comment job, which runs on the default branch and would only read its caches, declares cache-mode: write and pastes the comment body into a shell. Anyone who can comment runs code there. With the grant, the triage job saves its setup-go cache in the default branch's scope, the very key the push-triggered release job restores before running npm publish with NPM_TOKEN, so the comment body walks one hop along that cache edge into the release job: an untrusted expression reaching a secret and a publish, Critical. The grant itself (ISSUE-705) is the entry of a second path from the triage job into every job restoring a cache, whatever key it saves (the run's cache token can save any), entered by the comment body (anyone who can comment, nothing caps it): Critical too. Every action is pinned by SHA from GitHub's own owners, so no dependency path joins. Hand count: two Critical paths 2 x 35 = 70, no other finding, so 100 - 70 = 30: E.

sentenceContains: Code running in `triage/label` can write caches that `release/publish` restores
